selection_hint: Select four distinct exact CSL or near-pair markers in one axial layer, in perimeter order around a convex cell.

atom_counts.convention: half-open planar cell, one full axial repeat

warnings: This is a homogeneous geometric strain fit, not an elastic-energy minimum or relaxed grain boundary.
Coincidences and local pairs compare atoms in the same axial phase only.
The common cell preserves axial layers and is not necessarily primitive in three dimensions.

strain.convention: x_current = F_grain @ x_reference + translation; F uses unrotated analysis xy coordinates

edge_analysis.layer_policy: Search G1/G2 pairs within each axial layer separately, then retain all globally shortest nonzero pairs per edge across every layer. Never pair atoms from different layers.
edge_analysis.convention: Directed displacement G1→G2 in unrotated analysis coordinates; lengths in a0 and Angstrom. Lattice [uvw] coefficients use each grain's deformed conventional basis.
edge_analysis.edge_membership: Projected atoms exactly on each selected finite segment in every axial layer; no nearby band, visibility filter or viewport clipping.
edge_analysis.zero_pairs_policy: Equal rational edge fractions are coincident and excluded, including the selected corners.
edge_analysis.tie_policy: All exact minimum nonzero differences of rational edge fractions are retained, with their actual saved-transform displacements.
edge_analysis.interpretation: These geometric displacements are candidate secondary misfit Burgers vectors, not proof of a dislocation or a Burgers-circuit measurement.

provenance.purpose: Continue initial near-CSL setup for the Ni {110} || {111} grain boundary using the saved actual geometry. The user selects four near-CSL sites in the floating widget; after confirmation, Structure reads this request, applies strain, and reports the all-layer edge vectors as possible secondary misfit Burgers vectors.
